title: Simon Wiesenthal, a Holocaust survivor, collected evidence on Nazi criminals to bring them to justice

trailer.text: Simon Wiesenthal was a Jewish architect and Holocaust survivor who became known as the "Nazi hunter", according to HaMichlol.
According to the Simon Wiesenthal Center, he dedicated his life to ensuring that the crimes of the Nazi regime were not forgotten and that those responsible for them were brought to justice.
In the Holocaust, 89 members of his family and of his wife's family perished.
In 1947, together with thirty volunteers, he opened a documentation center in Linz, Austria, to assemble evidence for future trials.
He built a card index of 22,500 names and prepared dossiers on six thousand cases,
and when he died in Vienna at the age of 96, he was buried in Herzliya, Israel.

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: U.S. Congressional Gold Medal, French Legion of Honor

stations.title: A child from Buczacz, an architect from Prague

paragraphs.text: Simon Wiesenthal was born on December 31, 1908 in Buczacz, in an area that is now in the Lvov Oblast of Ukraine.
He grew up in a well-to-do Jewish family.
He wanted to study at the Polytechnic in Lvov, but was turned away because of quotas on Jewish students.
He therefore went to study in Prague, and in 1932 he received a degree in architectural engineering.
According to the Wiesenthal Center, he saved himself, his wife and his mother from deportation to Siberia by bribing an NKVD commissar.
Later he made a deal with the Polish underground: he handed over charts of railroad junctions, and in return received false papers for his wife.
In August 1942 his mother was sent to the Belzec death camp.
According to HaMichlol, on April 20, 1943 the Janowska guards decided to shoot 54 Jews to death, to mark Hitler's 54th birthday.
In October 1943 Wiesenthal escaped the Ostbahn labor camp with the help of the deputy director, shortly before the Germans began liquidating all the prisoners.
After he was recaptured in June 1944 and returned to the Janowska camp, the SS guards at the camp joined the general retreat westward with only 34 prisoners out of the 149,000 originally held there.
On May 5, 1945 an American armored unit liberated the Mauthausen camp, and Wiesenthal was then barely alive.
According to HaMichlol, he was 1.80 meters tall, and at the end of the war he weighed less than 45 kilograms.
As soon as his health was restored, Wiesenthal began gathering and preparing evidence on Nazi atrocities for the War Crimes Section of the United States Army.
Wiesenthal and his wife were reunited; until then, each had believed the other was dead.
A daughter, Pauline, was born to them.
In 1947 Wiesenthal and thirty volunteers opened the Jewish Historical Documentation Center in Linz, Austria, to assemble evidence for future trials.

According to the newspaper, when he opened the documentation center in Vienna following the capture of Eichmann in 1960, he at first had few financial resources and few political allies in his work as a Nazi hunter.
According to the encyclopedia, the onset of the Cold War made prosecuting Nazi criminals politically unattractive to the Western powers.
In 1954 the office in Linz was closed, and its files were given to the Yad Vashem Archives in Israel, except for one file.

stations.title: Eichmann, and the office in Vienna

paragraphs.text: According to the Wiesenthal Center, Adolf Eichmann was living in Buenos Aires under an alias.
Israeli agents captured him and brought him to Israel for trial.
According to the Wiesenthal Center, Eichmann was found guilty of mass murder and executed.
According to the news site JNS, the hanging was scheduled for midnight, was slightly delayed, and thus took place a few minutes past midnight on 1 June 1962.
According to the encyclopedia, the information Wiesenthal gathered on Eichmann assisted the Israeli authorities in his capture.
According to HaMichlol, Wiesenthal himself never claimed that he was the one who brought about Eichmann's capture.
After Eichmann's capture, Wiesenthal reopened the Jewish Documentation Center, this time in Vienna.
This time he concentrated only on hunting war criminals.

stations.title: How he worked: card index, dossiers and the press

paragraphs.text: Contrary to popular belief, Wiesenthal did not usually track down the Nazi fugitives himself.
His chief task was gathering and analyzing information.
According to HaMichlol, his method was based on the meticulous collection of every piece of information.
He compiled a card index of 22,500 names and prepared dossiers on six thousand cases.
At times he worked on as many as three hundred cases at once.
When the authorities did not act, Wiesenthal turned to the press and the media.
Experience had taught him that publicity and public outrage are a powerful weapon.
According to HaMichlol, he led an international pressure campaign, following which the West German parliament abolished the statute of limitations on Nazi crimes.
According to the EBSCO encyclopedia, he insisted that morality must remain on the side of the accusers, and that proper punishment can come only from the courts.
In 1963 Wiesenthal located Karl Silberbauer, then a police inspector in Austria.

Dutch neo-Nazi propagandists were fairly successful in their attempts to discredit the authenticity of Anne Frank's diary, until in 1963 Wiesenthal located Karl Silberbauer, then a police inspector in Austria.
According to the History website, Silberbauer was temporarily suspended from the Vienna police but was not prosecuted, because he was found to have acted only under orders.
In October 1966, sixteen SS officers went on trial in Stuttgart, West Germany, for participation in the extermination of the Jews of Lvov; nine of them had been located by Wiesenthal.
After three years of undercover work by Wiesenthal, Franz Stangl was located in Brazil, and in 1967 he was extradited to West Germany.
According to HaMichlol, Hermine Braunsteiner was arrested in Queens, New York, where she lived as a housewife.
She was arrested after lengthy research by Wiesenthal and by volunteers he sent.
According to the Wiesenthal Center, Hermine Ryan (née Braunsteiner) was extradited to Germany in 1973 and received life imprisonment.
The newspaper reported that Wiesenthal issued a worldwide appeal to save the documentation center in Vienna from possible closure by the Austrian government.

stations.title: Recognition, last words and resting place

paragraphs.text: In 1977 the Simon Wiesenthal Center for Holocaust Studies in Los Angeles was named after him.
In 1980 he received the U.S. Congressional Gold Medal from U.S. President Carter, and in 1986 he received the French Legion of Honor.

According to the EBSCO encyclopedia, he was nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize in 1985, received freedom medals from the Netherlands and from Luxembourg, and also received the Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Clinton.
Wiesenthal declined to join the ceremony at Bitburg, because SS soldiers were buried in the cemetery there.

According to Hamichlol, only in the 1990s did Austrian society return and reconcile with Wiesenthal, and the generation of the grandchildren of those who took part in the Second World War saw him as a symbol of democracy, integrity and sanity.
Wiesenthal wrote that survival is a privilege which entails obligations.
He also wrote that he constantly asks himself what he can do for those who did not survive.
In a 1994 interview he said that the only value of about five decades of his work is a warning to the murderers of tomorrow that they will never rest.
In 2003 he said in an interview with the Austrian weekly "Format" that he had found the mass murderers he had been looking for.
According to HaMichlol, Wiesenthal refused to immigrate to Israel, although his wife asked him to and although his daughter, son-in-law and grandchildren immigrated.
He died on September 20, 2005 at his home in Vienna, at the age of 96, and was buried in Herzliya, Israel.
Rabbi Marvin Hier said that Wiesenthal showed the world what one person determined to do the right thing can accomplish.
In 2006 the Vienna city government renamed a street Simon-Wiesenthal-Gasse in his honor.
According to HaMichlol, Wiesenthal's information on Mengele's whereabouts proved wrong.
The information led the searchers to Paraguay instead of Brazil, and drew criticism.
According to the EBSCO encyclopedia, a Canadian government commission concluded that the estimates of Nazi criminals in Canada had been grossly exaggerated.
According to the EBSCO encyclopedia, Holocaust survivors and Nazi hunters, among them Elie Wiesel, accused Wiesenthal of gross exaggeration in some of his claims.
According to HaMichlol, the hunter Tuviah Friedman called Wiesenthal a liar, a swindler and an anti-Zionist, and claimed that he had become famous and rich from fabricated stories.
According to the EBSCO encyclopedia, some Zionists saw his pursuit of justice against Nazis as detracting from their goals and sought to discredit his efforts.
Wiesenthal was engaged in a legal dispute with Austrian Chancellor Kreisky.
According to HaMichlol, the dispute broke out after Wiesenthal pointed to government members with a Nazi past.
In June 1982 a bomb exploded at the door of Wiesenthal's house and caused a great deal of damage; no one was hurt.
One German neo-Nazi and several Austrian neo-Nazis were arrested for the bombing.
The German was found to be the main perpetrator and was sentenced to five years in prison.

disagreements.question: How many camps was Wiesenthal in?

versions.says: According to the History website, he survived imprisonment in four concentration camps and a death march
According to the EBSCO encyclopedia, he survived a dozen concentration and death camps

disagreements.question: In what year was Wiesenthal reunited with his wife?

versions.says: According to the Wiesenthal Center, late in 1945
According to the History website, in 1947

disagreements.question: In what year was his daughter Pauline born?

versions.says: According to the Wiesenthal Center, in 1946
According to the EBSCO encyclopedia, in 1947
According to the encyclopedia, in Brazil in 1960
According to the Wiesenthal Center, in Buenos Aires

disagreements.question: What was Wiesenthal's role in locating Eichmann?

versions.says: According to the EBSCO encyclopedia, Wiesenthal first gained international recognition for locating Eichmann in Buenos Aires
According to the newspaper, experts say Wiesenthal was not instrumental in tracking down Eichmann, contrary to the popular perception
According to HaMichlol, former Mossad head Isser Harel claimed that Wiesenthal had no part in locating and capturing Eichmann

disagreements.question: How many criminals were brought to justice thanks to Wiesenthal?

versions.says: According to HaMichlol, Wiesenthal and his people brought about a thousand Nazi war criminals to trial
Elsewhere in HaMichlol it is written that he brought more than 1,100 war criminals to justice
According to the encyclopedia, he helped bring approximately eleven hundred war criminals to justice

disagreements.question: How many names were in the war criminal files in Germany?

versions.says: According to the Wiesenthal Center, more than 90,000 names, most of them of people who were never tried
According to the EBSCO encyclopedia, the West German government's files held more than 160,000 names, most of them never tried

disagreements.question: Who sued whom in the dispute with Kreisky?

versions.says: According to the EBSCO encyclopedia, Wiesenthal brought a libel suit against Kreisky, and eventually reached an out-of-court settlement
According to HaMichlol, it was Kreisky who threatened to sue Wiesenthal for libel

claims.quote: Dutch neo-Nazi propagandists were fairly successful in their attempts to discredit the authenticity of Anne Frank's famous diary until Wiesenthal located Silberbauer, then a police inspector in Austria, in 1963.

claims.quote: While he was temporarily suspended from the Vienna police force, he was not prosecuted. He was found to be only acting under orders from his commander.

claims.text: באוקטובר 1966 הועמדו לדין בשטוטגרט שישה עשר קציני אס אס, תשעה מהם נמצאו על ידי ויזנטל.
claims.quote: In October 1966, sixteen SS officers, nine of them found by Wiesenthal, went on trial in Stuttgart, West Germany, for participation in the extermination of Jews in Lvov.

claims.text: לאחר שלוש שנות עבודה חשאית של ויזנטל אותר פרנץ שטנגל בברזיל והוסגר למערב גרמניה ב-1967.
claims.quote: After three years of patient undercover work by Wiesenthal, Stangl was located in Brazil and remanded to West Germany for imprisonment in 1967.

claims.text: לפי המכלול, בראונשטיינר נעצרה בקווינס שבניו יורק, שם חייתה כעקרת בית, לאחר מחקר ממושך של ויזנטל ומתנדבים שנשלחו על ידו.
claims.quote: לאחר מחקר ממושך של ויזנטל ומתנדבים שונים שנשלחו על ידו, היא נעצרה ברובע קווינס שבניו יורק, שם חייתה כעקרת בית.

claims.text: הרמינה ראיין (לבית בראונשטיינר) הוסגרה לגרמניה ב-1973 וקיבלה מאסר עולם, לפי מרכז ויזנטל.
claims.quote: She was extradited to Germany for trial as a war criminal in 1973 and received life imprisonment.

claims.text: בעיתון נכתב שוויזנטל פנה בקריאה עולמית לסייע להציל את מרכז התיעוד בווינה מסגירה אפשרית על ידי ממשלת אוסטריה.
claims.quote: has issued a worldwide appeal to help save his Documentation Center in Vienna from what he fears is imminent closure by the Austrian government

claims.text: ב-1977 נקרא מרכז שמעון ויזנטל ללימודי שואה בלוס אנג'לס על שמו.
claims.quote: In 1977 the Simon Wiesenthal Center for Holocaust Studies in Los Angeles was named in his honor.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית אבסקו, ויזנטל קיבל גם מועמדות לפרס נובל לשלום ב-1985, מדליות חירות הולנדית ולוקסמבורגית ואת מדליית החירות הנשיאותית מנשיא קלינטון.
claims.quote: a Nobel Peace Prize nomination in 1985, membership in the French Legion of Honor in 1986, the Dutch Freedom Medal, the Luxembourg Freedom Medal

claims.text: ויזנטל סירב להצטרף לטקס בביטבורג כי חיילי אס אס היו קבורים בבית הקברות.
claims.quote: Wiesenthal declined because SS soldiers were buried in the cemetery where the ceremony took place.

claims.text: לפי המכלול, בשנות ה-90 הפכה החברה האוסטרית לרואה בוויזנטל סמל לדמוקרטיה, ליושר ולשפיות.
claims.quote: דור הנכדים של משתתפי מלחמת העולם השנייה ראה בוויזנטל סמל לדמוקרטיה, ליושר ולשפיות.

claims.text: ויזנטל כתב שההישרדות היא זכות שמטילה חובות, ושהוא שואל את עצמו כל העת מה יוכל לעשות למען מי שלא שרדו.
claims.quote: Survival is a privilege which entails obligations. I am forever asking myself what I can do for those who have not survived.

claims.text: ויזנטל אמר בראיון ב-1994 שהערך היחיד של כחמישה עשורי עבודתו הוא אזהרה לרוצחי המחר שלעולם לא ינוחו.
claims.quote: The only value of nearly five decades of my work is a warning to the murderers of tomorrow, that they will never rest.

claims.text: ב-2003 אמר ויזנטל בראיון לשבועון האוסטרי "פורמט" שגילה את הרוצחים ההמוניים שחיפש.
claims.quote: גיליתי את הרוצחים ההמוניים שחיפשתי והארכתי חיים יותר מכולם.

claims.text: לפי המכלול, ויזנטל סירב לעלות לישראל למרות בקשות אשתו ועלייתם של בתו, חתנו ונכדיו.
claims.quote: סירב ויזנטל לעלות לישראל, למרות בקשותיה של אשתו ולמרות עלייתם של בתו, חתנו ונכדיו.

claims.text: הרב מרווין הייר מילא את הדברים: ויזנטל הראה לעולם מה יכול אדם אחד נחוש לעשות את הדבר הנכון להשיג.
claims.quote: Simon Wiesenthal showed the world what one person determined to do the right thing can accomplish

claims.text: ב-2006 שינתה עיריית וינה שם של רחוב ל-Simon-Wiesenthal-Gasse לכבודו.
claims.quote: In 2006 the Vienna city government renamed a street, Simon-Wiesenthal-Gasse, in his honor.

claims.text: לפי המכלול, המידע של ויזנטל על מקום הימצאו של מנגלה התברר כשגוי והוביל את המחפשים לפרגוואי במקום לברזיל, מה שעורר ביקורת.
claims.quote: המידע שסיפק על מקום הימצאו של יוזף מנגלה התברר כשגוי. מידע זה הוביל את המחפשים אחרי מנגלה לפרגוואי במקום לברזיל

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית אבסקו, ועדה ממשלתית בקנדה קבעה שההערכות על מספר הפושעים הנאצים בקנדה הוגזמו מאוד.
claims.quote: a Canadian government commission appointed to study the evidence concluded that the estimates of Nazi criminals in Canada had been grossly exaggerated

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית אבסקו, ניצולי שואה וציידי נאצים, ובהם אלי ויזל, האשימו את ויזנטל בהגזמה חמורה בחלק מטענותיו.
claims.quote: some fellow Holocaust survivors and Nazi hunters, including Nobel laureate Elie Wiesel, accused Wiesenthal of gross exaggeration in some of his claims

claims.text: לפי המכלול, הצייד טוביה פרידמן כינה את ויזנטל שקרן, נוכל ואנטי-ציוני וטען שהתפרסם והתעשר מסיפורי בדים.
claims.quote: צייד הנאצים טוביה פרידמן, שעבד תקופה מסוימת עם ויזנטל, כינה אותו שקרן, נוכל ואנטי-ציוני, וטען שהתפרסם והתעשר מסיפורי בדים על לכידת אייכמן ונאצים אחרים.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית אבסקו, ציונים מסוימים ראו בחתירתו של ויזנטל לצדק כלפי נאצים פוגעת ביעדיהם וניסו להכפיש את מאמציו.
claims.quote: Some Zionists considered his ecumenical, justice-based pursuit of former Nazis to detract from their parochial goals and sought to discredit his efforts.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית אבסקו, ויזנטל הגיש תביעת דיבה נגד הקנצלר קרייסקי ולבסוף הגיע להסדר מחוץ לבית המשפט.
claims.quote: Relations between the two degenerated to personal invective, until Wiesenthal finally brought a libel suit against the chancellor.

claims.text: לפי המכלול, קרייסקי הוא שאיים לתבוע את ויזנטל בגין דיבה לאחר שהצביע על חברי ממשלה בעלי עבר נאצי.
claims.quote: איים לתבוע את ויזנטל למשפט דיבה, לאחר שוויזנטל הצביע על כמה מחברי ממשלתו כבעלי עבר נאצי

claims.text: ביוני 1982 התפוצצה פצצה בדלת ביתו של ויזנטל וגרמה נזק רב, ואיש לא נפגע.
claims.quote: In June 1982, a bomb exploded at the front door of his house causing a great deal of damage. Fortunately, no one was hurt.

claims.text: בגין הפיצוץ נעצרו נאו-נאצי גרמני וכמה נאו-נאצים אוסטרים, והגרמני, שנמצא המבצע העיקרי, נידון לחמש שנות מאסר.
claims.quote: One German and several Austrian neo-Nazis were arrested for the bombing. The German, who was found to be the main perpetrator, was sentenced to five years in prison.

claims.text: לפי אתר הסטורי, ויזנטל שרד מאסר בארבעה מחנות ריכוז ובצעדת מוות.
claims.quote: as he lived through imprisonment in four concentration camps and a death march

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית אבסקו, ויזנטל שרד תריסר מחנות ריכוז והשמדה נאציים.
claims.quote: Wiesenthal, a survivor of a dozen Nazi concentration and death camps, became the leading independent Nazi hunter.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית אבסקו, ויזנטל זכה להכרה בינלאומית לראשונה על איתור אייכמן בבואנוס איירס.
claims.quote: Wiesenthal first gained international recognition for locating Eichmann in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

claims.text: לפי העיתון, מומחים אומרים שוויזנטל לא היה מכריע באיתור אייכמן, בניגוד לתפיסה הרווחת.
claims.quote: Despite the popular perception, experts say Wiesenthal was not instrumental in tracking down Eichmann.

claims.text: לפי המכלול, ראש המוסד לשעבר איסר הראל טען שלוויזנטל לא היה חלק באיתור ובתפיסת אייכמן.
claims.quote: ראש המוסד לשעבר איסר הראל טען, כאמור, כי לוויזנטל לא היה כל חלק באיתור ותפיסת אדולף אייכמן

claims.text: לפי המכלול, ויזנטל ואנשיו הביאו למשפט כאלף פושעי מלחמה נאצים.
claims.quote: בסך הכול הצליחו ויזנטל ואנשיו להביא למשפט כאלף פושעי מלחמה נאצים.

claims.text: לפי המכלול, ויזנטל הצליח להביא לדין יותר מ-1,100 פושעי מלחמה.
claims.quote: הוא הצליח להביא לדין יותר מ-1,100 פושעי מלחמה שהיו אחראים לרציחות המוניות בעת השואה.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה, ויזנטל סייע להביא לדין כאחד עשר מאות פושעי מלחמה.
claims.quote: In total, Wiesenthal helped bring approximately eleven hundred war criminals to justice.

claims.text: לפי מרכז ויזנטל, תיקי פושעי המלחמה של גרמניה כוללים יותר מ-90,000 שמות, רובם של אנשים שמעולם לא נשפטו.
claims.quote: Germany's war criminal files contain more than 90,000 names, most of them of people who have never been tried.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית אבסקו, בתיקי פשעי המלחמה של ממשלת מערב גרמניה היו יותר מ-160,000 שמות, רובם לא נשפטו.
claims.quote: The West German government had more than 160,000 names in its war-crimes files, most of them never tried.

claims.text: לפי אתר החדשות JNS, התלייה נקבעה לחצות, התעכבה מעט, ולכן התקיימה כמה דקות אחרי חצות, ב-1 ביוני 1962.
claims.quote: The hanging, scheduled for midnight, was slightly delayed and thus took place a few minutes past midnight on 1 June 1962.

quote_translations.c2: Was a Jewish architect who became known as the "Nazi hunter". As a Holocaust survivor, he dedicated his life to collecting and documenting information about Nazi war criminals
quote_translations.c63: On September 20, 2005 he died at his home in Vienna at the age of 96. He was buried in the cemetery in Herzliya in Israel.
quote_translations.c3: He was born in 1908 to a well-to-do Jewish family in the town of Buczacz, which lies today in Ukraine, and as he grew up he moved to Prague and studied architecture
quote_translations.c12: On April 20, 1943, to mark Hitler's 54th birthday, the Janowska guards decided to shoot 54 Jews to death in a celebration
quote_translations.c13: Although he was 1.80 meters tall, he weighed less than 45 kilograms.
quote_translations.c26: Wiesenthal never claimed that he brought about the capture of Adolf Eichmann.
quote_translations.c35: Wiesenthal never engaged in the physical hunting of war criminals. His working method was based on the meticulous collection of every possible scrap of paper and item of information
quote_translations.c64: and he also led an international pressure campaign that caused the West German parliament to abolish the statute of limitations on Nazi crimes
quote_translations.c32: After lengthy research by Wiesenthal and various volunteers sent by him, she was arrested in the borough of Queens in New York, where she lived as a housewife.
quote_translations.c66: The generation of the grandchildren of those who took part in World War II saw Wiesenthal as a symbol of democracy, integrity and sanity.
quote_translations.c62: I found the mass murderers I was looking for and I outlived them all.
quote_translations.c69: Wiesenthal refused to immigrate to Israel, despite his wife's requests and despite the immigration of his daughter, son-in-law and grandchildren.
quote_translations.c33: The information he provided on the whereabouts of Josef Mengele proved wrong. This information led those searching for Mengele to Paraguay instead of Brazil
quote_translations.c55: Nazi hunter Tuviah Friedman, who worked with Wiesenthal for a certain period, called him a liar, a swindler and an anti-Zionist, and claimed that he had become famous and rich from fabricated stories about the capture of Eichmann and other Nazis.
quote_translations.c53: threatened to sue Wiesenthal for libel, after Wiesenthal pointed to several members of his government as having a Nazi past
quote_translations.c25: Former Mossad head Isser Harel claimed, as noted, that Wiesenthal had no part whatsoever in locating and capturing Adolf Eichmann
quote_translations.c37: In all, Wiesenthal and his people succeeded in bringing about a thousand Nazi war criminals to trial.
quote_translations.c38: He succeeded in bringing to justice more than 1,100 war criminals who were responsible for mass murders during the Holocaust.
